tagline: Across the hill towns, past mill foundations and a covered river crossing.
intro: The Route 116 Scenic Byway crosses the hills from Adams to South Deerfield, with views toward Mount Greylock in Cheshire and a winding course through Conway. Western Massachusetts Scenic Byways highlights the country road’s open spaces and historic town centers as evidence of the region’s agricultural and industrial past. Plainfield’s village center occupies flatter ground between steep rises and falls to the east and west.

One change in the road helped shape Conway itself. The early meetinghouse and taverns stood beside the South River along an east–west road north of today’s Route 116. In 1832, the main road shifted south, and the present center began to develop. Forty percent of the district’s buildings date from the boom years of the 1840s and 1850s, chiefly in Greek Revival style.

Begin in Adams’s Hoosic River valley and head through the northeast corner of Cheshire into Savoy. Continue east through Plainfield to Ashfield, where Route 116 briefly shares Route 112. Beyond Ashfield, pass the Burkeville Covered Bridge near Conway, then follow the winding road through Conway toward South Deerfield, the byway’s eastern end.

moments.title: Adams
moments.text: Susan B. Anthony’s childhood home gives Adams a connection to the Quaker families who settled here in the 1760s. Anthony, the abolitionist and suffragist, was born in Adams in 1820. Her house at 67 East Road was built in 1817 and is now a museum devoted to her early years. Twin chimneys rise from its center line, and much of the original woodwork and the central-hall floor plan remain. The house passed out of the family in 1895, became a museum in 1926, returned to private ownership, and underwent restoration from 2006 to 2009.

moments.title: Plainfield
moments.text: Cellar holes, mill foundations, small cemeteries and old apple orchards are the subjects of Plainfield’s five self-guided Hidden Walls, Hidden Mills walks. They lead through fields and farms. In its early years, the agricultural town had gristmills and sawmills serving local needs. The village center also gained a water company in 1816, with an aqueduct supplying water through wooden pipes. Along Main Street, Route 116 passes a historic district containing the town hall of 1847 and library of 1925; its oldest houses are mostly Cape-style wooden buildings from the 1780s.

moments.title: Burkeville Covered Bridge
moments.text: Wooden trusses and wrought-iron vertical rods share the work at Burkeville Covered Bridge. The crossing stands just south of Route 116 over the South River, west of Conway’s center. Built in 1870 after the preceding bridge suffered flood damage, it has needed repeated repairs. The 1938 hurricane weakened it, and heavy snow partly collapsed the roof in 1975; town volunteers restored the roof. A gabled metal roof and vertical boards cover the structure, while steel components reinforce or replace some truss fittings.
moments.notice: Vertical board siding and a gabled metal roof enclose the bridge.
